Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model (e.g. Haiku) running in the
  background typically suffices, which is what the config is for:

  ```yaml
  references:
    transcription:
      harness: <optional harness>
      model: <cheap vision-capable model, e.g. a Haiku-class model>
  ```

  Don't pick the model inside the prompt; pin it in config so every transcription
  uses the same cheap vision model. When unset it falls back to the subagent/Ground
  harness.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.
- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

## The manifest at a glance

One entry per source (the `reference-retriever` owns the full schema):

```yaml
references:
  - slug: <slug>
    title: <title>
    source: <arXiv ID / DOI / URL>
    status: ok            # or: not_found
    files:
      - { path: <slug>/<slug>.pdf, format: pdf }
      - { path: <slug>/source.tex, format: tex }        # if TeX obtained
      - { path: <slug>/tex/page-0042.tex, format: tex } # if transcribed
    read: "Read TeX when present; else page anchors slug:page-NNNN. page_offset: ..."
```

If a source can't be found and verified, it's recorded `status: not_found` — treat
that as "no citation available," and write no math attributed to it.

Related skills: `blueprint-conventions` for where `\source{...}` sits among the
other blueprint annotations, and `leandag` for how a node's `sources` feed the DAG.

9	import Mathlib.RingTheory.FinitePresentation

11	/-!
12	# Presented étale covers of an affine base
13	
14	A (singleton, affine) *étale cover* of `Spec A` is a faithfully flat étale `A`-algebra `B`.
15	For the étale-sheafification (plus) construction of the relative Picard functor, the covers
16	of a fixed base must form a *small* directed index: this file realizes them as **presented**
17	covers — a number of variables `n` together with an ideal of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` whose
18	quotient is étale over `A` with `Spec` mapping onto `Spec A`.  The type of presented covers
19	of `A` lives in the same universe as `A`, while still capturing every étale cover up to
20	isomorphism of the carrier (`Algebra.EtaleCover.of` and its accessor `ofEquiv`).
21	
22	Surjectivity of the spectrum map is recorded instead of faithful flatness because it is
23	statable without flatness hypotheses; combined with flatness of étale algebras it *is*
24	faithful flatness (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_comap_surjective`), and that instance is
25	provided on the carrier.
26	
27	## Main declarations
28	
29	* `Algebra.EtaleCover A`: presented étale covers of `Spec A`, a `Type u` for `A : Type u`;
30	  `E.Carrier` is the covering algebra, with `Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier` and
31	  `Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier` instances.
32	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.of B hB`: any étale `A`-algebra `B` (with surjective spectrum map)
33	  underlies a presented cover, with carrier identification `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv`.
34	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines`: `E'` refines `E` when the covering spectrum of `E'` maps
35	  to that of `E` over the base — a mere existence (`Prop`); the plus construction proves
36	  independence of the chosen refinement map, so no choice of map is carried here.
37	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.prod`: the common refinement `Spec (B ⊗[A] B')` of two covers, with
38	  refinement witnesses `prodInl`/`prodInr` — directedness of the index
39	  (`exists_refines_prod`).
40	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.self`: the trivial cover `Spec A` itself, refined by every cover
41	  (`refines_self`) — the base point of the index.
42	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`: the pulled-back cover along `A → A'`, with carrier
43	  `A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (`baseChangeEquiv`) and the canonical `A`-algebra map
44	  `baseChangeInclude` into it.
45	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`: over a field `K`, every cover
46	  is refined by a finite separable field extension of `K` (single-factor refinement) —
47	  field-extension covers are cofinal, the form the degree theory and Galois descent
48	  consume; `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField` packages such an extension as a cover.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open TensorProduct
56	
57	namespace Algebra
58	
59	/-- A presented étale cover of `Spec A`: a finite-variable polynomial presentation of an
60	étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum maps onto `Spec A`.  Presentations keep the type of covers
61	small (`Type u` for `A : Type u`), which is what makes the étale plus construction over
62	these covers a legitimate colimit; the carrier-level content is recovered by
63	`Algebra.EtaleCover.of`/`ofEquiv`. -/
64	structure EtaleCover (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Type u where
65	  /-- The number of variables of the presentation. -/
66	  n : ℕ
67	  /-- The ideal of relations of the presentation. -/
68	  ideal : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
69	  /-- The presented algebra is étale over the base. -/
70	  etale : Algebra.Etale A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)
71	  /-- The spectrum of the presented algebra covers the spectrum of the base. -/
72	  comap_surjective :
73	    Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)))
74	
75	namespace EtaleCover
76	
77	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
78	
79	/-- The covering algebra presented by an étale cover. -/
80	protected abbrev Carrier (E : EtaleCover A) : Type u :=
81	  MvPolynomial (Fin E.n) A ⧸ E.ideal
82	
83	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier :=
84	  E.etale
85	
86	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier :=
87	  .of_comap_surjective E.comap_surjective
88	
89	/-! ## Constructors -/
90	
91	section constructors
92	
93	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
94	
95	/-- Package an explicitly presented étale algebra with surjective spectrum map as a
96	presented étale cover: the ideal of relations is the kernel of the presenting
97	surjection. -/
98	noncomputable def ofSurjective
99	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
100	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
101	    EtaleCover A where
102	  n := n
103	  ideal := RingHom.ker f
104	  etale := .of_equiv (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).symm
105	  comap_surjective := by
106	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A B := .of_comap_surjective hB
107	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ RingHom.ker f) :=
108	      .of_linearEquiv A B (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).toLinearEquiv
109	    exact PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
110	
111	/-- The carrier of `ofSurjective` is the presented algebra. -/
112	noncomputable def ofSurjectiveEquiv
113	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
114	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
115	    (ofSurjective hB f hf).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
116	  Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf
117	
118	/-- Any étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum covers `Spec A` underlies a presented étale
119	cover.  The presentation is chosen (étale algebras are finitely presented, in particular
120	finitely generated); the choice is harmless because consumers only ever use the carrier
121	identification `ofEquiv`. -/
122	noncomputable def of (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
123	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) : EtaleCover A :=
124	  ofSurjective hB
125	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose
126	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose_spec
127	
128	/-- The carrier of `of B hB` is `B` itself. -/
129	noncomputable def ofEquiv (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
130	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) :
131	    (of B hB).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
132	  ofSurjectiveEquiv hB _ _
133	
134	end constructors
135	
136	/-! ## Refinement and directedness -/
137	
138	/-- `E'` refines `E`: the covering spectrum of `E'` maps to that of `E` over `Spec A`,
139	i.e. there is an `A`-algebra map from the carrier of `E` to that of `E'`.  This is a mere
140	existence: the plus construction proves that the induced maps on descent classes do not
141	depend on the chosen refinement map, so no map is carried here. -/
142	def Refines (E' E : EtaleCover A) : Prop :=
143	  Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E'.Carrier)
144	
145	theorem refines_refl (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines E :=
146	  ⟨AlgHom.id A E.Carrier⟩
147	
148	theorem Refines.trans {E E' E'' : EtaleCover A} (h : E''.Refines E') (h' : E'.Refines E) :
149	    E''.Refines E := by
150	  obtain ⟨f⟩ := h
151	  obtain ⟨g⟩ := h'
152	  exact ⟨f.comp g⟩
153	
154	/-- The common refinement of two covers: `Spec` of the tensor product of the carriers,
155	i.e. the fiber product of the covering spectra over the base. -/
156	noncomputable def prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A :=
157	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
158	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
159	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
160	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
161	  .of (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
162	
163	/-- The carrier of the common refinement is the tensor product of the carriers. -/
164	noncomputable def prodEquiv (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
165	    (E.prod E').Carrier ≃ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier :=
166	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
167	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
168	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
169	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
170	  ofEquiv (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
171	
172	/-- The first refinement map of the common refinement. -/
173	noncomputable def prodInl (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
174	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
175	
176	/-- The second refinement map of the common refinement. -/
177	noncomputable def prodInr (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
178	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
179	
180	/-- Combine refinement maps out of the two factors into one out of the common
181	refinement (the universal property of the fiber product of the covering spectra). -/
182	noncomputable def prodLift {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
183	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (E.prod E').Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier :=
184	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f g fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _).comp
185	    (E.prodEquiv E').toAlgHom
186	
187	@[simp]
188	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInl {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
189	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInl E') = f := by
190	  ext x
191	  simp [prodLift, prodInl]
192	
193	@[simp]
194	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInr {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
195	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInr E') = g := by
196	  ext x
197	  simp [prodLift, prodInr]
198	
199	theorem prod_refines_left (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E :=
200	  ⟨E.prodInl E'⟩
201	
202	theorem prod_refines_right (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E' :=
203	  ⟨E.prodInr E'⟩
204	
205	/-- Directedness of the refinement preorder: any two covers have a common refinement. -/
206	theorem exists_refines_prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
207	    ∃ E'' : EtaleCover A, E''.Refines E ∧ E''.Refines E' :=
208	  ⟨E.prod E', E.prod_refines_left E', E.prod_refines_right E'⟩
209	
210	/-- The trivial cover of `Spec A` by itself. -/
211	noncomputable def self (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : EtaleCover A :=
212	  .of A (by
213	    rw [show algebraMap A A = RingHom.id A from rfl, PrimeSpectrum.comap_id]
214	    exact fun p => ⟨p, rfl⟩)
215	
216	/-- The carrier of the trivial cover is the base ring. -/
217	noncomputable def selfEquiv (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : (self A).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] A :=
218	  ofEquiv A _
219	
220	/-- The canonical refinement map from the trivial cover to any cover (algebra side: the
221	structure map of the carrier, through the trivial carrier's identification with `A`). -/
222	noncomputable def fromSelf (E : EtaleCover A) : (self A).Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier :=
223	  (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).comp (selfEquiv A).toAlgHom
224	
225	/-- Every cover refines the trivial cover: the trivial cover is the base point of the
226	refinement preorder. -/
227	theorem refines_self (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines (self A) :=
228	  ⟨E.fromSelf⟩
229	
230	/-! ## Base change -/
231	
232	section baseChange
233	
234	variable (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A']
235	
236	/-- The base change of a cover along `A → A'`: the cover of `Spec A'` with carrier
237	`A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (the fiber product of the covering spectrum with the new base). -/
238	noncomputable def baseChange (E : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A' :=
239	  .of (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
240	
241	/-- The carrier of the base-changed cover is the base-changed carrier. -/
242	noncomputable def baseChangeEquiv (E : EtaleCover A) :
243	    (E.baseChange A').Carrier ≃ₐ[A'] A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
244	  ofEquiv (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
245	
246	/-- The canonical map from the carrier of a cover to the carrier of its base change,
247	as a map of `A`-algebras. -/
248	noncomputable def baseChangeInclude (E : EtaleCover A) :
249	    E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.baseChange A').Carrier :=
250	  (((E.baseChangeEquiv A').symm.toAlgHom).restrictScalars A).comp
251	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
252	
253	/-- The base change of a refinement map: `A' ⊗[A] —` on carriers, through the
254	presented-carrier identifications — the functoriality of `baseChange` in the cover. -/
255	noncomputable def baseChangeMap {E F : EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
256	    (E.baseChange A').Carrier →ₐ[A'] (F.baseChange A').Carrier :=
257	  ((F.baseChangeEquiv A').symm.toAlgHom).comp
258	    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A' A') h).comp (E.baseChangeEquiv A').toAlgHom)
259	
260	/-- Base change of refinement maps commutes with the canonical inclusions into the base
261	change. -/
262	theorem baseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeInclude {E F : EtaleCover A}
263	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
264	    ((baseChangeMap A' h).restrictScalars A).comp (E.baseChangeInclude A')
265	      = (F.baseChangeInclude A').comp h := by
266	  ext x
267	  simp [baseChangeMap, baseChangeInclude]
268	
269	end baseChange
270	
271	/-! ## Covers of a field: single-factor refinement -/
272	
273	section field
274	
275	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
276	
277	/-- The carrier of a cover of a field (indeed, of any nontrivial base) is nontrivial. -/
278	theorem nontrivial_carrier (E : EtaleCover A) [Nontrivial A] : Nontrivial E.Carrier :=
279	  PrimeSpectrum.nonempty_iff_nontrivial.mp
280	    ⟨(E.comap_surjective (Nonempty.some inferInstance)).choose⟩
281	
282	/-- **Field cofinality**: over a field, every presented étale cover is refined by a finite
283	separable field extension.  This single-factor refinement is what makes field-extension
284	covers cofinal among étale covers of `Spec K`: the étale carrier is a finite product of
285	finite separable extensions of `K`, and projection to any one factor still covers the
286	(one-point) spectrum of `K`. -/
287	theorem exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom (E : EtaleCover K) :
288	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L)
289	      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L), Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L) := by
290	  haveI : Nontrivial E.Carrier := E.nontrivial_carrier

9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard functor on affine test algebras
11	
12	The étale sheafification of the relative Picard functor is computed over *affine* test
13	objects, where a test object is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra `A` (the landed
14	`AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A : Over (Spec k)`) and a test map is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
15	map.  This file provides the algebra-indexed face of the relative Picard functor:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.overSpecMap f`: `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map `f : A →ₐ[k] B`, as a
18	  morphism `overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A` of `Over (Spec k)`, strictly functorial
19	  (`overSpecMap_id`, `overSpecMap_comp`).
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap C f`: restriction of relative Picard classes along
21	  `Spec f`, a group homomorphism `relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B)`,
22	  covariantly functorial in the algebra (`relPicAlgMap_id`, `relPicAlgMap_comp`).
23	
24	The étale plus construction (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`) consumes only this interface: descent
25	classes on an étale cover are an equalizer of two `relPicAlgMap`s, and all refinement
26	transports are `relPicAlgMap`s of `A`-algebra maps restricted to `k`.
27	-/

45	  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom)) (by

55	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom) = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := by

62	            Spec (CommRingCat.of C') ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of B))

88	noncomputable def relPicAlgMap (f : A →ₐ[k] B) :
89	    relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B) :=

9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/
43	
44	set_option autoImplicit false
45	
46	universe u
47	
48	open CategoryTheory
49	
50	open scoped TensorProduct
51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
53	
54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
55	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
56	
57	noncomputable section
58	
59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
60	
61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
67	
68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
72	
73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
75	cover. -/
76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))
81	
82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
87	  Iff.rfl
88	
89	/-! ## Transport along refinement maps -/
90	
91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
94	  ext x
95	  simp [doubleInl]
96	
97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
100	  ext x
101	  simp [doubleInr]
102	
103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
125	
126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2
131	
132	@[simp]
133	lemma descentMap_coe {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
134	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
135	    (descentMap C h x : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
136	      = relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
137	  rfl
138	
139	@[simp]
140	lemma descentMap_id {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (x : descentClasses C E) :
141	    descentMap C (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier) x = x := by
142	  ext
143	  rw [descentMap_coe,
144	    show (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k = AlgHom.id k E.Carrier from rfl]
145	  exact relPicAlgMap_id C _
146	
147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
150	  ext
151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]
154	  exact relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
155	
156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
168	    ext y
169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
171	    ext y
172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
180	        rw [hx']
181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]
184	
185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
187	all choices. -/
188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)
192	
193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
194	
195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
201	  iseqv := by
202	    constructor
203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]
211	
212	variable (A) in
213	/-- The one-step étale plus of the relative Picard functor at the affine test `Spec A`:
214	relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
215	modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
216	sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
217	étale-separated — proved separately). -/
218	def PicEtAff : Type u :=
219	  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))
220	
221	namespace PicEtAff
222	
223	/-- The plus class of a relative Picard class with a descent condition on a cover. -/
224	def mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) : PicEtAff C A :=
225	  Quotient.mk _ ⟨E, x⟩
226	
227	@[elab_as_elim]
228	theorem ind {motive : PicEtAff C A → Prop}
229	    (mk : ∀ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E), motive (mk C E x)) :
230	    ∀ q, motive q := by
231	  intro q
232	  induction q using Quotient.ind with
233	  | _ p => exact mk p.1 p.2
234	
235	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
236	    {y : descentClasses C F} :
237	    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
238	      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
239	        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=
240	  Quotient.eq
241	
242	/-- Transporting the representative to a finer cover does not change the plus class. -/
243	@[simp]
244	theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
245	    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
246	  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩
247	
248	/-! ### The group structure -/
249	
250	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
251	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
252	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
253	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
254	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
255	      = descentMap C f x := by
256	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]
257	
258	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the right factor. -/
259	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inr {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
260	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
261	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
262	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)
263	      = descentMap C g y := by
264	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInr]
265	
266	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
267	-- The `rw` chain unifies `descentMap` nests whose `AlgHom` instance arguments run through
268	-- quotient and tensor-product carriers; the unifications are heartbeat-hungry.
269	private lemma mulLift_compat (p q p' q' : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E)
270	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') :
271	    mk C (p.1.prod q.1)
272	        (descentMap C (p.1.prodInl q.1) p.2 * descentMap C (p.1.prodInr q.1) q.2)
273	      = mk C (p'.1.prod q'.1)
274	        (descentMap C (p'.1.prodInl q'.1) p'.2
275	          * descentMap C (p'.1.prodInr q'.1) q'.2) := by

8	/-!
9	# Functoriality of the étale plus construction in the test algebra
10	
11	The étale-plus Picard group `PicEtAff C A` is functorial in the affine test: a base
12	extension `A → A'` restricts a plus class by base-changing its representing cover
13	(`Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`) and transporting the descent datum along the canonical
14	inclusion of the carrier into its base change.  Following the mathlib idiom for maps along
15	base extensions, the extension is carried as instances `[Algebra A A'] [IsScalarTower k A A']`
16	rather than as an explicit `k`-algebra map.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentBaseChange C A' E`: transport of descent classes along the base
19	  change of the cover — well-posed because the two coprojections of the base-changed double
20	  cover restrict to `A`-algebra maps out of the original carrier, so the keystone
21	  `relPicAlgMap_congr` applies.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map C A'`: the induced restriction homomorphism
23	  `PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A'`.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_unit`: naturality of the unit of the plus construction.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_id`, `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_map`: the functor
26	  laws — both are instances of `relPicAlgMap_congr`, which erases the difference between
27	  any two transports out of the same descent class.
28	
29	Together with the unit (`PicEtAff.unit`), this is the presheaf structure of the one-step
30	étale plus of the relative Picard functor on affine tests; the comparison theorems
31	(separatedness, rigidification under a section) consume this interface.
32	-/

50	/-! ## Transport of descent classes along base change of the cover -/
51	
52	/-- The descent condition survives base change of the cover: the two coprojections of the
53	base-changed double cover restrict along the canonical inclusion to `A`-algebra maps out
54	of the original carrier, so `relPicAlgMap_congr` identifies the two pullbacks. -/
55	lemma baseChangeInclude_mem_descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
56	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
57	    relPicAlgMap C ((E.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k) x
58	      ∈ descentClasses C (E.baseChange A') := by
59	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
60	  have h₁ : (doubleInl (E.baseChange A')).comp ((E.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
61	      = (((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (S := A')).restrictScalars A).comp
62	          (E.baseChangeInclude A')).restrictScalars k :=
63	    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
64	  have h₂ : (doubleInr (E.baseChange A')).comp ((E.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
65	      = (((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars A).comp
66	          (E.baseChangeInclude A')).restrictScalars k :=
67	    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
68	  rw [h₁, h₂]
69	  exact relPicAlgMap_congr C _ _ hx

71	/-- Transport of descent classes along the base change of the cover. -/
72	def descentBaseChange (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
73	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C (E.baseChange A') :=
74	  ((relPicAlgMap C ((E.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)).comp
75	    (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
76	    fun x => baseChangeInclude_mem_descentClasses C A' E x.2
77	
78	@[simp]
79	lemma descentBaseChange_coe (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
80	    (descentBaseChange C A' E x : relPic C (overSpec k (E.baseChange A').Carrier))
81	      = relPicAlgMap C ((E.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
82	          (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
83	  rfl
84	
85	/-- Base-change transport commutes with refinement transport — the naturality square that
86	makes the transport descend to the plus quotient. -/
87	lemma descentMap_baseChangeMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
88	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
89	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' h) (descentBaseChange C A' E x)
90	      = descentBaseChange C A' F (descentMap C h x) := by
91	  have hcomp : ((Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' h).restrictScalars k).comp
92	        ((E.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
93	      = ((F.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) := by
94	    have := Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeInclude A' h
95	    calc ((Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' h).restrictScalars k).comp
96	          ((E.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
97	        = ((((Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' h).restrictScalars A).comp
98	            (E.baseChangeInclude A')).restrictScalars k) := AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
99	      _ = (((F.baseChangeInclude A').comp h).restrictScalars k) := by rw [this]
100	      _ = ((F.baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) :=
101	          AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
102	  ext
103	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentBaseChange_coe, descentBaseChange_coe, descentMap_coe,
104	    ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, hcomp]

110	private def mapSig (p : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) :
111	    Σ E' : Algebra.EtaleCover A', descentClasses C E' :=
112	  ⟨p.1.baseChange A', descentBaseChange C A' p.1 p.2⟩
113	
114	/- Stated with the sigma pairs fully destructured, so that no goal ever mentions a
115	sigma-literal projection. -/
116	private lemma mapSig_rel {E F' : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
117	    {y : descentClasses C F'} (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
118	    (g : F'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (hfg : descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y) :
119	    ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A')
120	      (f' : (E.baseChange A').Carrier →ₐ[A'] G.Carrier)
121	      (g' : (F'.baseChange A').Carrier →ₐ[A'] G.Carrier),
122	      descentMap C f' (descentBaseChange C A' E x)
123	        = descentMap C g' (descentBaseChange C A' F' y) :=
124	  ⟨F.baseChange A', Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' f,
125	    Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' g, by
126	      rw [descentMap_baseChangeMap, descentMap_baseChangeMap, hfg]⟩
127	
128	private lemma mapSig_compat {p q : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E}
129	    (h : p ≈ q) : mapSig C A' p ≈ mapSig C A' q := by
130	  obtain ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ := h
131	  exact mapSig_rel C A' F f g hfg

133	private def mapFun : PicEtAff C A → PicEtAff C A' :=
134	  Quotient.map (mapSig C A') fun _ _ h => mapSig_compat C A' h

136	private lemma mapFun_mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
137	    mapFun C A' (mk C E x) = mk C (E.baseChange A') (descentBaseChange C A' E x) :=
138	  rfl

141	    mapFun C A' (a * b) = mapFun C A' a * mapFun C A' b := by
142	  induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
143	  induction b using ind with | _ F y =>
144	  have h₁ : mapFun C A' (mk C E x)
145	      = mk C ((E.prod F).baseChange A')
146	          (descentBaseChange C A' (E.prod F) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)) := by
147	    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x, mapFun_mk]
148	  have h₂ : mapFun C A' (mk C F y)
149	      = mk C ((E.prod F).baseChange A')
150	          (descentBaseChange C A' (E.prod F) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)) := by
151	    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y, mapFun_mk]
152	  rw [mk_mul_mk, mapFun_mk, map_mul, ← mk_mul_mk_same, h₁, h₂]
153	
154	/-- Restriction of étale-plus Picard classes along a base extension `A → A'` of affine
155	tests: base-change the representing cover and transport the descent datum along the
156	canonical inclusion of the carrier into its base change. -/
157	def map : PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A' :=
158	  MonoidHom.mk' (mapFun C A') (mapFun_mul C A')

162	    map C A' (mk C E x) = mk C (E.baseChange A') (descentBaseChange C A' E x) :=

166	
167	/-- The unit of the plus construction is natural in the test algebra. -/
168	theorem map_unit (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
169	    map C A' (unit C A x)
170	      = unit C A' (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x) := by
171	  have hj : (((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k).comp
172	        ((Algebra.ofId A (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).Carrier).restrictScalars k)
173	      = ((((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf).restrictScalars k).comp
174	          (((Algebra.ofId A' (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A').Carrier).restrictScalars k).comp
175	            (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A')) := by
176	    ext a
177	    simp only [AlgHom.coe_comp, AlgHom.coe_restrictScalars', Function.comp_apply,
178	      Algebra.ofId_apply, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom', AlgHom.commutes]
179	    exact IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply A A' _ a
180	  have hval : relPicAlgMap C
181	        (((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
182	        (relPicAlgMap C
183	          ((Algebra.ofId A (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).Carrier).restrictScalars k) x)
184	      = relPicAlgMap C
185	          ((((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf).restrictScalars k)
186	          (relPicAlgMap C
187	            ((Algebra.ofId A' (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A').Carrier).restrictScalars k)
188	            (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x)) := by
189	    rw [← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, hj,
190	      AlgHom.comp_assoc]
191	  calc map C A' (unit C A x)
192	      = mk C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A')
193	          (descentMap C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf
194	            ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A')
195	              (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x)⟩) :=
196	        congrArg (mk C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A')) (Subtype.ext hval)
197	    _ = mk C (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A')
198	          ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A')
199	            (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x)⟩ :=
200	        mk_descentMap C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf _
201	    _ = unit C A' (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x) := rfl

66	## 2. (A) The definitional Pic carrier
67	
68	**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology
69	`Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site: covers by opens, unit-valued 1-cocycles modulo
70	coboundaries, colimit over refinement. This is recon lesson 1 verbatim, and it is Kleiman's own
71	remark `rk:coh` (§2.11): "for any ringed space `R`, there is a natural isomorphism
72	`Pic(R) = H¹(R, 𝒪_R^*)`" (his eq. 2.11.2 = `eq:2b`, citing Hartshorne III Ex. 4.5).
73	
74	**Semantic-honesty remark (record in the blueprint chapter).** The frozen `Challenge.lean` never
75	mentions `Pic`, line bundles, or invertible sheaves; the only consumers of the carrier are the
76	functors and elements defined in this spec. Therefore the comparison
77	"`CechPic X ≃ {invertible 𝒪_X-modules}/≅`" is **Phase-2 optional** (a `ForMathlib` PR
78	candidate), and no Wave depends on it. What is **Phase-1 mandatory** is that `𝒪(D)`-classes of
79	relative effective divisors be constructible as explicit cocycles from local equations, because
80	`ofCurve` is pinned as `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` (route §3). §2.6 pins that constructor.
81	
82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
89	```
90	
91	with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
92	
93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
102	  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
103	  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
104	  (pullback collapses indices).
105	- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
108	  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.

138	    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :

154	### 2.3 The refinement colimit
155	
156	```lean
157	/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
158	def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
159	  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
160	    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
161	```
162	
163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
164	  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
165	  choice-free.
166	- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
167	  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
168	- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
169	  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
170	- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
171	  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
172	  `CechPic (Spec (.of K)) ≃* PUnit`-style triviality for fields (one-point space, one cover,
173	  `ev_refl` kills every cocycle) — this is Lane 1's cheap end-to-end test.

175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178	
179	1. The cocycle values are *units of rings*; their native structure is multiplicative, and
180	   `tensor product of line bundles = pointwise multiplication of transition units`,
181	   `dual = pointwise inverse` — recon lesson 1's entire point. An additive carrier would
182	   re-introduce a translation layer at exactly the spot the old draft burned.
183	2. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` takes `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}` — multiplicative — and
184	   `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` is the canonical bridge. The old draft's
185	   `AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}` choice cost both a universe bump and an additive/multiplicative
186	   mismatch at the representability gate.
187	3. Mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1` layer (§2.2) is multiplicative.
188	
189	The `ℤ`-valued *degree* (§6) is additive; the interface between the multiplicative Pic and the
190	additive degree is a single `→ ℤ` map with `deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b` — pinned as such, no
191	`Multiplicative ℤ` gymnastics in consumer-facing statements.

194	
195	```lean
196	def Scheme.CechPic.map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic
197	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_id (X) : CechPic.map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id _
198	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
199	    CechPic.map (f ≫ g) = (CechPic.map f).comp (CechPic.map g)
200	```

206	friction appears, prove it through the refinement relation (both sides restrict to a common

209	### 2.6 Divisor classes as cocycles: the `𝒪(D)` constructor
210	
211	Three constructors, in dependency order. Sign convention (route §3, audited in §8):
212	a local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective `D` produces the class of `𝒪(D)` with
213	transition units `g x y = f x / f y` on overlaps (trivialization of `𝒪(D)` on `𝒰x` by
214	multiplication by `f x`).
215	
216	**(a) Local-equation data → class** (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean`):
217	
218	```lean
219	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor, adapted to a pointed cover. -/
220	structure Scheme.LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
221	  cover : X.PointedCover
222	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
223	  regular : ∀ x, /- eqn x is a nonzerodivisor in every stalk over cover.opens x -/
224	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, IsUnit (/- (eqn x)/(eqn y) as a section on the overlap, i.e.
225	      ∃ u : unit on 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y, (eqn x)|∩ = u * (eqn y)|∩ -/)
226	
227	def Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass (d : X.LocalEquations) : X.CechPic
228	  -- the class of the cocycle (x,y) ↦ the unit u x y with (eqn x)|∩ = u x y • (eqn y)|∩
229	```
230	
231	with: uniqueness of `u x y` (regularity makes the ratio unit unique — this is why `regular` is
232	part of the data), the cocycle identity for `u` (from associativity of the ratios),
233	*independence*: two `LocalEquations` cutting out the same closed subscheme (or related by
234	unitwise rescaling) have equal `picClass`; *multiplicativity*: pointwise product of equations ↦
235	product of classes; *pullback compatibility*: for `f : X' ⟶ X` such that the pulled-back
236	equations are still regular (guaranteed in the relative situation below),
237	`(d.pullback f).picClass = CechPic.map f d.picClass`.

241	- *Point divisor.* For a `k`-point `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C`, the image of `P` is an

5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic
6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Pullbacks
7	
8	/-!
9	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
10	
11	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
12	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
13	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
14	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
15	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
16	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
17	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
18	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
19	
20	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
21	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
22	of the challenge statement file.
23	
24	## Main declarations
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
27	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
29	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
30	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
31	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
33	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
35	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
36	-/
37	
38	set_option autoImplicit false
39	
40	universe u
41	
42	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
43	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)
44	
45	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
46	
47	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
48	
49	noncomputable section
50	
51	/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
52	along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
53	def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
54	  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range
55	
56	lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
57	    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
58	  Iff.rfl
59	
60	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
61	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
62	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
63	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T
64	
65	noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
66	  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)
67	
68	/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
69	noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
70	    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
71	  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)
72	
73	lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
74	    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
75	  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)
76	
77	/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
78	relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
79	lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
80	    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
81	    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
82	  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem
83	
84	@[elab_as_elim]
85	theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
86	    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
87	    motive x :=

89	
90	variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
91	
92	/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
93	from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
94	lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
95	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
96	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
97	  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
98	  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
99	      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
100	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
101	    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]
102	
103	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
104	`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
105	noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
106	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
107	    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)
108	
109	@[simp]
110	lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
111	    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
112	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
113	
114	lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
115	  induction x using relPic.ind with
116	  | mk L =>
117	    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
118	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
119	    rfl
120	
121	lemma relPicMap_comp (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T') (x : relPic C T) :
122	    relPicMap C (h ≫ g) x = relPicMap C h (relPicMap C g x) := by
123	  induction x using relPic.ind with
124	  | mk L =>
125	    rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk]
126	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C T'') ?_
127	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
128	      ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]
129	
130	/-- The relative Picard functor `T ↦ Pic(C ⊗ T)/Pic(T)` of Grothendieck–Kleiman, as a
131	presheaf of commutative groups on `Over (Spec k)`. -/
132	noncomputable def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
133	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop)
134	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMap C g.unop)
135	  map_id T := by
136	    ext x
137	    exact relPicMap_id C x
138	  map_comp g h := by
139	    ext x
140	    exact relPicMap_comp C g.unop h.unop x
141	
142	@[simp]
143	lemma relPicFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
144	    (relPicFunctor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop) :=
145	  rfl
146	
147	@[simp]
148	lemma relPicFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
149	    (x : relPic C T.unop) :
150	    (relPicFunctor C).map g x = relPicMap C g.unop x :=
151	  rfl
152	
153	/-! ## Naturality in the curve -/
154	
155	variable {C} {C' C'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
156

160	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C' T).comap (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) := by

163	  show CechPic.map (snd C' T).left N

168	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along a morphism of curves `g : C' ⟶ C`,

1261	Finally, there are two appendices.  Appendix A contains detailed answers
1262	to all the exercises.  Appendix B develops basic divisorial intersection
1263	theory, which is used freely throughout Section 6.  The treatment is
1264	short, simple, and elementary.
1265	
1266	\section{The several Picard functors}\label{sc:Pfctrs}
1267	\renewcommand{\theequation}{\thethm.\arabic{equation}}
1268	Our first job is to identify a likely candidate for the functor of
1269	points of the Picard scheme.  In fact, there are several reasonable such
1270	Picard functors, and each one is more likely to be representable than
1271	the preceding.  In this section, they all are formally introduced and
1272	compared.
1273	
1274	\begin{dfn}\label{df:aPf}
1275	 The {\it absolute Picard functor} $\Pic_X$ is the functor from  the
1276	 category of (locally Noetherian) $S$-schemes $T$ to the category of
1277	abelian groups defined by the formula
1278		$$\Pic_X(T):=\Pic(X_T).$$
1279	\end{dfn}
1280	
1281	The absolute Picard functor  is a ``prepared presheaf'' in this
1282	sense: given any family of  $S$-schemes $T_i$, we have
1283		$$\Pic_X\bigl(\textstyle\coprod T_i\bigr)=\prod\Pic_X(T_i).$$
1284	 Hence, given a covering family $\{T_i\to T\}$ in the Zariski topology,
1285	the \'etale topology, or any other Grothendieck topology on the category
1286	of $S$-schemes, there is no harm, when we consider the sheaf associated
1287	to $\Pic_X$, in working simply with the single map $T'\to T$ where
1288	$T':=\coprod T_i$.  And doing so lightens the notation, making for
1289	easier reading. Therefore, we do so throughout, calling $T'\to T$ simply
1290	a {\it covering\/} in the given topology.
1291	
1292	The absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$ is never a separated presheaf in
1293	the Zariski topology.  Indeed, take an $S$-scheme $T$ that carries an
1294	invertible sheaf $\mc N$ such that $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.  (For
1295	example, take $T:=\I P^1_X$ and $\mc N:=\mc O_{\!T}(1)$.  Then the diagonal
1296	map $X\to X\x X$ induces a section $g$ of $f_T$; that is, $gf_T=1_T$.
1297	Hence $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.)  Now, there exists a Zariski covering
1298	$T'\to T$ such that the pullback $\mc N|T'$ is trivial; here, $T'$ is
1299	simply the disjoint union of the subsets in a suitable ordinary open
1300	covering of $T$.  So the pullback $f^*_{T'}\mc N|X_{T'}$ is trivial too.
1301	Thus $\Pic_X(T)$ has a nonzero element whose restriction is zero in
1302	$\Pic_X(T')$.
1303	
1304	According to descent theory, every representable functor is a sheaf in
1305	the Zariski topology \emdash in fact, in the \'etale and fppf
1306	topologies as well.  Therefore, the absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$ is never
1307	representable.  So, in the hope of obtaining a representable functor
1308	that differs as little as possible from $\Pic_X$, we now define a
1309	sequence of three successively more promising relative functors.
1310	
1311	\begin{dfn}\label{df:Pfs}
1312	  The {\it relative Picard functor} $\Pic_{X/S}$ is defined by
1313		$$\Pic_{X/S}(T):=\Pic(X_T)\big/\Pic(T).$$
1314	 Denote its associated sheaves in the Zariski, \'etale, and fppf
1315	topologies  by
1316		$$\Pic_{(X/S)\zar},\ \Pic_{(X/S)\et},\
1317		\Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}.$$
1318	 \end{dfn}
1319	
1320	We now have a sequence of five Picard functors, and each one maps
1321	naturally into the next.  So each one maps naturally into any of its
1322	successors.  If the latter functor is one of the three just displayed,
1323	then it is a sheaf in the indicated topology; in fact, it is the sheaf
1324	associated to any one of its predecessors, and the map between them is
1325	the natural map from a presheaf to its associated sheaf, as is easy to
1326	check.  In particular, the three displayed sheaves are the sheaves
1327	associated to the absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$, as well as to the
1328	relative Picard functor $\Pic_{X/S}$.
1329	
1330	Since $\Pic_{X/S}$ is not a priori a sheaf, it is remarkable that it is
1331	representable so often in practice.
1332	
1333	Note that, for every $S$-scheme $T$, each $T$-point of
1334	$\Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}$, or element of $\Pic_{(X/S)\fpqc}(T)$, is
1335	represented by an invertible sheaf $\mc L'$ on $X_{T'}$ for some
1336	fppf-covering $T'\to T$.    Moreover, there must
1337	be an fppf-covering $T''\to T'\x_T T'$ such that the two pullbacks of
1338	$\mc L'$ to $X_{T''}$ are isomorphic \emdash or to put it informally, the
1339	restrictions of $\mc L'$ must agree on a covering of the overlaps.
1340	
1341	Furthermore, a second such sheaf $\mc L_1$ on $X_{T_1}$ represents the
1342	same $T$-point if and only if there is an fppf-covering $T_1'\to T_1\x_T
1343	T'$ such that the pullbacks of $\mc L'$ and $\mc L_1$ to $X_{T_1'}$ are
1344	isomorphic.  Technically, this condition includes the preceding one,
1345	which concerns the case where $T_1=T'$ and $\mc L_1=\mc L'$ since $\mc
1346	L'$ must represent the same $T$-point as itself.  Of course, similar
1347	considerations apply to the Picard functors for the Zariski and \'etale
1348	topologies as well.

1360	Assume $A$ is an algebraically closed  field $k$.  Show

1365	 Show that the natural map
1366		$$\Pic_{(X/S)\zar}\to \Pic_{(X/S)\et}$$

1369		$$X:u^2+v^2+w^2=0 \text{ in }\I P^2_\bb R.$$

74	  and \(s \subset N\) a finite subset such that:
75	  \begin{enumerate}
76	    \item \(s \subseteq Q_0\);
77	    \item \(s\) spans \(N\) over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\): \(\langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\);

79	      \(x \in Q_0\);
80	    \item \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\): \(T^{-1} \cdot x \in Q_1\) for
81	      all \(x \in Q_1\);
82	    \item every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_1\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\)
83	      with \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\).
84	  \end{enumerate}

86	  monomials \(T^j \cdot x\), for \(x \in s\) and \(-M < j < 0\), where \(M\) is any uniform
87	  bound with \(T^{-M} \cdot x \in Q_1\) for every \(x \in s\).
88	\end{theorem}
89	\begin{proof}
90	  \leanok
91	  \uses{lem:T_pow_stable, lem:T_inv_pow_stable}

93	  \(m_x \ge 0\) with \(T^{-m_x} \cdot x \in Q_1\); let \(M = \max_{x \in s} m_x\) (or \(M = 0\)
94	  if \(s\) is empty). For each \(x \in s\), since \(M - m_x \ge 0\) and \(Q_1\) is stable
95	  under \(T^{-1}\), Lemma~\ref{lem:T_inv_pow_stable} gives
96	  \[
97	    T^{-M} \cdot x = T^{-(M - m_x)} \cdot \bigl(T^{-m_x} \cdot x\bigr) \in Q_1 ,
98	  \]
99	  so \(M\) is a uniform bound for all of \(s\).
100	
101	  Let \(F = \{\, T^j \cdot x : x \in s,\ -M < j < 0 \,\}\), a finite subset of \(N\) (finite
102	  since \(s\) is finite and \(j\) ranges over the \(M - 1\) integers strictly between \(-M\)
103	  and \(0\)).
104	
105	  \emph{Claim.} For every \(x \in s\) and every \(j \in \Z\),
106	  \(T^j \cdot x \in Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\), where \(\langle F \rangle_k\) is the
107	  \(k\)-submodule generated by \(F\).
108	
109	  Indeed, if \(j \ge 0\), then since \(x \in s \subseteq Q_0\) and \(Q_0\) is stable under
110	  \(T\), Lemma~\ref{lem:T_pow_stable} gives \(T^j \cdot x \in Q_0\). If \(j \le -M\), write
111	  \(j = -d - M\) with \(d = -j - M \ge 0\); then
112	  \[

114	  \]
115	  and since \(T^{-M} \cdot x \in Q_1\) and \(Q_1\) is stable under \(T^{-1}\),
116	  Lemma~\ref{lem:T_inv_pow_stable} gives \(T^j \cdot x \in Q_1\). Finally, if \(-M < j < 0\),
117	  then \(T^j \cdot x \in F \subseteq \langle F \rangle_k\) by definition of \(F\). This proves
118	  the claim.

120	  Every element \(f \in k[T,T^{-1}]\) is, by definition of the Laurent polynomial ring, a
121	  \(k\)-linear combination of finitely many monomials \(T^j\), \(j \in \Z\). Since
122	  \(Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\) is a \(k\)-submodule of \(N\), the claim and this
123	  decomposition of \(f\) give, for every \(x \in s\),
124	  \[

126	  \]

129	  in \(Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\) by the previous paragraph, and this submodule is
130	  closed under addition, so \(n \in Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\). Hence
131	  \[
132	    Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k = N .
133	  \]

135	  N/(Q_0+Q_1)\) is surjective, so the (finite) image of \(F\) in \(N/(Q_0+Q_1)\) spans it as a
136	  \(k\)-module. Thus \(N/(Q_0+Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.
137	\end{proof}

140	
141	The spanning-set form of Theorem~\ref{thm:two_lattice_span} is inconvenient when only a
142	localization-type hypothesis on \(Q_0\) is available, symmetric to hypothesis (5) on \(Q_1\):
143	every element of \(N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_0\) after multiplying by a sufficiently
144	large power of \(T\). The next two results derive the finiteness conclusion from this
145	symmetric pair of hypotheses, at the cost of assuming \(N\) itself is a finite
146	\(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module; this is exactly the shape of hypothesis produced by localizing a
147	finite module away from an element.

155	  canonical ring map \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\). Let \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be \(k\)-submodules

159	    \item \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\);
160	    \item every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_0\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\)
161	      with \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\);
162	    \item every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_1\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\)
163	      with \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\).
164	  \end{enumerate}
165	  Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.
166	\end{corollary}
167	\begin{proof}
168	  \leanok
169	  \uses{thm:two_lattice_span}
170	  Since \(N\) is a finite \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module, choose a finite subset \(t \subset N\) with
171	  \(\langle t \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\). By hypothesis (3), for each \(y \in t\) choose an

178	  The set \(s\) again spans \(N\) over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\): each element of \(s\) is a
179	  \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-multiple of an element of \(t\), so

181	  \(T\) is invertible in \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) with inverse \(T^{-1}\), every \(y \in t\) is
182	  recovered from \(s\) by
183	  \[

185	  \]

187	  \(t \subseteq \langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]}\), giving
188	  \(\langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} \supseteq \langle t \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\) as well.

1	\chapter{The \'etale plus construction of the relative Picard functor}
2	\label{chap:PicardEtale}
3	
4	For a curve \(C\) over \(k\) and an affine test scheme \(\Spec A\), the \'etale-sheafified
5	relative Picard group is computed by a single \emph{plus construction}: a class is represented
6	by a relative Picard class on an \'etale cover of \(\Spec A\) satisfying a descent condition,
7	and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common refinement. This chapter
8	constructs that plus, on affine test schemes indexed by a \(k\)-algebra \(A\); we recall from
9	elsewhere in this project the ambient functor it sheafifies. For an object \(T\) of
10	\(\Over(\Spec k)\) write \(\mathrm{relPic}(C,T)\) for the relative Picard group of \(C\) at
11	\(T\) --- the quotient of the Picard group of \(C \otimes T\) by the subgroup of classes pulled
12	back from \(T\) along the second projection --- a commutative group, with restriction
13	homomorphisms \(g^{*} \colon \mathrm{relPic}(C,T) \to \mathrm{relPic}(C,T')\) for a morphism
14	\(g \colon T' \to T\) of \(\Over(\Spec k)\), satisfying \((\id_T)^{*} = \id\) and
15	\((g \circ h)^{*} = h^{*} \circ g^{*}\). For a commutative \(k\)-algebra \(A\), write \(\Spec A\)
16	also for the object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\) it determines via the structure morphism
17	\(\Spec A \to \Spec k\) induced by the \(k\)-algebra structure of \(A\); a homomorphism of
18	\(k\)-algebras \(A \to A'\) induces, via \(\Spec\), a morphism \(\Spec A' \to \Spec A\) of
19	\(\Over(\Spec k)\). We abbreviate \(\mathrm{relPic}(C,A) := \mathrm{relPic}(C,\Spec A)\).
20	
21	\section{Presented \'etale covers of an affine scheme}
22	
23	Throughout this section \(A\) is a commutative ring (no field or \(k\)-algebra structure is
24	needed here). An \'etale cover of \(\Spec A\) in the sense consumed by the plus construction is
25	a faithfully flat \'etale \(A\)-algebra; to keep the index of covers of a fixed base
26	small --- which is what makes the plus construction below a legitimate colimit, rather than one
27	indexed by a proper class of isomorphism types --- we realize such algebras through an explicit
28	finite-variable presentation, at the cost of carrying a witness of the presentation as data.
29	
30	\begin{definition}[Presented \'etale cover]
31	  \label{def:etale_cover}
32	  \lean{Algebra.EtaleCover, Algebra.EtaleCover.Carrier}
33	  \leanok
34	  A \emph{presented \'etale cover} \(E\) of \(A\) consists of a natural number \(n\), an ideal
35	  \(I\) of the polynomial ring \(A[x_1,\dots,x_n]\), a proof that the quotient algebra
36	  \(B_E := A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/I\) is \'etale over \(A\), and a proof that the induced map of
37	  spectra \(\Spec B_E \to \Spec A\) is surjective. We call \(B_E\) the \emph{carrier} of \(E\).
38	  Since \'etale algebras are flat, surjectivity of \(\Spec B_E \to \Spec A\) together with
39	  flatness makes \(B_E\) faithfully flat over \(A\).
40	\end{definition}
41	
42	\begin{definition}[Presented covers from an \'etale algebra]
43	  \label{def:etale_cover_of}
44	  \lean{Algebra.EtaleCover.of}
45	  \uses{def:etale_cover}
46	  \leanok
47	  Let \(B\) be an \'etale \(A\)-algebra such that \(\Spec B \to \Spec A\) is surjective. Since
48	  \'etale algebras are of finite presentation, \(B\) admits a presentation as a quotient of a
49	  polynomial ring in finitely many variables over \(A\); choosing one such presentation
50	  produces a presented \'etale cover \(E\) of \(A\), denoted \(E = \mathrm{of}(B)\).
51	\end{definition}
52	
53	\begin{lemma}[Carrier of a presented cover from an algebra]
54	  \label{lem:etale_cover_ofEquiv}
55	  \lean{Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv}
56	  \uses{def:etale_cover_of}
57	  \leanok
58	  In the situation of Definition~\ref{def:etale_cover_of}, the carrier \(B_E\) of
59	  \(E = \mathrm{of}(B)\) is isomorphic to \(B\) as an \(A\)-algebra.
60	\end{lemma}
61	\begin{proof}
62	  \leanok
63	  Immediate from the construction: \(E\) is built from a chosen presentation
64	  \(A[x_1,\dots,x_n] \twoheadrightarrow B\), and the carrier of the resulting cover is the
65	  quotient of \(A[x_1,\dots,x_n]\) by the kernel of that presentation, which is isomorphic to
66	  \(B\) by the first isomorphism theorem for algebras.
67	\end{proof}
68	
69	\begin{definition}[Refinement]
70	  \label{def:etale_cover_refines}
71	  \lean{Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines}
72	  \uses{def:etale_cover}
73	  \leanok
74	  For presented \'etale covers \(E, E'\) of \(A\), we say \(E'\) \emph{refines} \(E\) if there
75	  exists a homomorphism of \(A\)-algebras \(B_E \to B_{E'}\) (equivalently, a morphism
76	  \(\Spec B_{E'} \to \Spec B_E\) over \(\Spec A\)). This is a mere existence statement: no
77	  particular refinement map is remembered as data.
78	\end{definition}
79	
80	\begin{lemma}[Refinement is a preorder]
81	  \label{lem:etale_cover_refines_preorder}
82	  \lean{Algebra.EtaleCover.refines_refl, Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines.trans}
83	  \uses{def:etale_cover_refines}
84	  \leanok
85	  Every presented \'etale cover \(E\) of \(A\) refines itself, and if \(E''\) refines \(E'\)
86	  and \(E'\) refines \(E\) then \(E''\) refines \(E\).
87	\end{lemma}
88	\begin{proof}
89	  \leanok
90	  Reflexivity: the identity homomorphism of \(B_E\) witnesses that \(E\) refines itself.
91	  Transitivity: composing a homomorphism \(B_{E'} \to B_{E''}\) witnessing that \(E''\) refines
92	  \(E'\) with a homomorphism \(B_E \to B_{E'}\) witnessing that \(E'\) refines \(E\) gives a
93	  homomorphism \(B_E \to B_{E''}\) witnessing that \(E''\) refines \(E\).
94	\end{proof}
95	
96	\begin{definition}[Common refinement]
97	  \label{def:etale_cover_prod}
98	  \lean{Algebra.EtaleCover.prod, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodEquiv}
99	  \uses{def:etale_cover_of}
100	  \leanok
101	  For presented \'etale covers \(E, E'\) of \(A\), the \emph{common refinement} \(E \times E'\)
102	  is the presented \'etale cover of \(A\) with carrier \(B_E \otimes_A B_{E'}\) (\'etale over
103	  \(A\) because it is \'etale over the \'etale algebra \(B_E\), which is \'etale over \(A\); and
104	  faithfully flat by transitivity of faithfully flat extensions), obtained by applying
105	  Definition~\ref{def:etale_cover_of} to \(B_E \otimes_A B_{E'}\).
106	\end{definition}
107	
108	\begin{definition}[Coprojections of the common refinement]
109	  \label{def:etale_cover_prod_coproj}
110	  \lean{Algebra.EtaleCover.prodInl, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodInr}
111	  \uses{def:etale_cover_prod}
112	  \leanok
113	  The two canonical homomorphisms of \(A\)-algebras

116	  identification of Definition~\ref{def:etale_cover_prod}.
117	\end{definition}
